content:
The image shows opened soybean pods with seeds. Key observations:
- Seeds are shriveled, flat, and underdeveloped
- Visible white fluffy/cottony growth among and on seeds
- Pod walls appear bleached white
- Some seeds appear replaced or coated by white mycelial material
- Dark bodies (sclerotia) are visible mixed among seeds

This matches **White_Mold** precisely:
- "pods contain smaller, lighter, cottony seeds"
- "infected seeds may be flat, shriveled, or replaced by sclerotia"
- "white fluffy mycelial growth" on infected tissue
- "hard, black sclerotia... on or inside stems and pods"
- Bleached white pod walls consistent with "infected stems become soft, watery, and bleached white"

No other class fits — Phomopsis seeds are cracked/gray mold but lack white fluffy mycelium; Downy_mildew shows whitish mass on seeds but without sclerotia.

```json
{"prediction": "White_Mold", "confidence": 0.92, "reasoning": "Opened pods show shriveled/flat seeds with white fluffy cottony mycelial growth and dark sclerotia embedded among seeds, with bleached white pod walls — all hallmark signs of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum)."}
```
